title: Text Embedding Model
description: Encoder model mapping text sequences into high-dimensional vector representations.
name: Text Embedding Model
summary: Text Embedding Models are bi-directional transformer encoders trained using contrastive objectives to represent semantic text concepts as dense floating-point vector coordinates in high-dimensional spaces.
use_when: Building semantic search indexes, RAG vector retrievers, or clustering text datasets.
avoid_when: Generating text responses or dialogues, as encoders cannot generate tokens autoregressively.
pros: Extremely fast to compute compared to decoder generation.
Accurately captures semantic similarity regardless of exact keyword matches.
Enables sub-millisecond retrieval of context documents from vector databases.
cons: Strict limit on input text sequence length (typically 512 or 8192 tokens).
Embeddings represent average meaning, losing details in very long texts.
Requires a separate vector database indexing and search layer.

key_hyperparams.name: normalize_embeddings
key_hyperparams.note: Whether to normalize output vectors to unit length. Allows using simple dot products for cosine similarity.

quick_start:
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
sentences = ["Hello World", "Semantic text embedding"]
embeddings = model.encode(sentences)
